clue.text: Chap meeting old lover by bay is a pirate captain

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase naming a role; the answer is the captain himself

parts.note: a chap is a gent, a man
leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart
bay is a reddish-brown colour, especially of horses

explanation.surface: A man takes up with a former sweetheart at the seaside and turns out to be a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: GENT, then LEMAN (an old word for lover), then BROWN for bay. The answer is the pirate in Conrad's Lord Jim.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentleman Brown is the buccaneer chief who raids Patusan in Joseph Conrad's novel Lord Jim.

clue.text: Writer of comedy gold about Italy

parts.note: taken as written
on means about, concerning
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Praise for a playwright whose comedy is pure gold.
explanation.walkthrough: GOLD, then ON for 'about' and I for Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlo Goldoni was the eighteenth-century Venetian playwright famed for comedies like The Servant of Two Masters.

clue.text: Butler's lover with a canny style in disguise

indicators.note: letters in disguise are rearranged so the original words cannot be recognised

explanation.surface: A servant's sweetheart is cunningly dressed up to hide who she is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' is not a manservant but the novelist Samuel Butler; rearrange A CANNY STYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Astley is the girl loved in a Samuel Butler story, the author named rather than a household servant.

clue.text: End up following the French lady in a Keats poem

indicators.note: following puts the turned-up piece after the French article

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A finishing note about a French woman who features in a Romantic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' looks like a verb meaning finish, but it is a noun: a goal. 'Up' turns it round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamia is the serpent-woman heroine of Keats's narrative poem of that title.

clue.text: This character in a history play injures a Shakespearean prince

definitions.text: This character in a history play

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage, so mars means injures
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's Henry IV plays

explanation.surface: A figure in one of Shakespeare's histories wounds the young heir to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: MARS for 'injures', then HAL, the prince of Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Marshal is an officer who presides over the trial by combat in Shakespeare's Richard II.

clue.text: Old story in which Albert, possibly from Camden, is an entertaining person on the up

parts.note: Camden is a city in New Jersey, abbreviated NJ, so 'from Camden' gives the state
Al is a short form of Albert, among other names
is shortened to 's

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the up means these pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an is the article a
someone who is a gas is great fun, an entertaining person

explanation.surface: An ancient tale in which a man called Albert from north London turns out to be a riot and goes up in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Camden suggests the London borough, but it is Camden, New Jersey: NJ. Then AL, S ('s for is), and A GAS read upwards, which makes SAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Njal's Saga is a thirteenth-century Icelandic prose epic, an old narrative of feuds.

clue.text: Indian author, extremely ready to consume bummalo, in the end

indicators.note: to consume means the outer letters swallow the other piece
extremely asks for the extremes, the first and last letters of ready
in the end points to the final letter of bummalo

explanation.surface: A writer from India keen to eat a fish dish once the meal is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: R and Y, the first and last letters of 'ready', take in O, the end of 'bummalo' (Bombay duck, a fish).
explanation.definitionFit: Arundhati Roy is the Indian novelist who won the Booker Prize for The God of Small Things.

clue.text: Revolutionary police supported by an East European author with his own printing press

definitions.text: author with his own printing press

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by puts the second piece underneath the first
revolutionary means turned round, so the word for police is read backwards

parts.note: the law is slang for the police
a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: Radical officers backed by a man from Poland, a writer who printed his own books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests an anagram of 'police', but it turns a synonym round; the law is slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace Walpole ran a private press at his Strawberry Hill house, printing his friends' poems and his own works.

clue.text: Scandalous novelist's temptingly naughty content

indicators.note: content as a noun is what something holds, so the letters inside the phrase are taken

explanation.surface: A racy writer's books are full of seductively wicked material.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' linking definition and wordplay; 'content' reads as the material of the books but signals letters held within.
explanation.definitionFit: Elinor Glyn's romantic novels, notably Three Weeks, caused a sensation for their racy content in Edwardian times.

clue.text: She loved a man who wrote about Our Lady and Christmas

definitions.text: She loved a man who wrote
definitions.note: the definition is a description of a woman, a character in a novel

parts.note: Marian means relating to the Virgin Mary, Our Lady
Yule is an old name for Christmas

explanation.surface: A woman devoted to a writer of devotional pieces about the Virgin and the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gissing's New Grub Street, Marian Yule loves the writer Jasper Milvain.
explanation.definitionFit: Marian Yule, in George Gissing's novel, is a literary drudge in love with the ambitious journalist Jasper Milvain.

clue.text: Funny play with Moth — one with a wide range of roles?

definitions.text: one with a wide range of roles?

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A comic drama featuring a character called Moth, played by a versatile actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange PLAY and MOTH. Moth is a page in Love's Labour's Lost, which helps the theatrical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A polymath is a person of wide learning across many subjects, playfully pictured as an actor of many parts.

clue.text: Jack, a traveller on horseback in a book about London

definitions.meaning: a jack or jack tar is a seaman

definitions.text: a traveller on horseback in a book about London
definitions.meaning: Irving Stone's biography of the writer Jack London is titled ... on Horseback

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the title of Irving Stone's biography of Jack London, which gives the first word its double sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman is called a jack, and Stone's life of Jack London called him a seafarer on horseback.

clue.text: Novelist from Scotland, or a town belonging to another country

parts.note: Irvine is a town in Ayrshire in Scotland, and also a city in California
Welsh means belonging to Wales, another country of the UK

explanation.surface: A writer from Scotland, or perhaps a place that belongs to a neighbouring nation.
explanation.walkthrough: IRVINE, a Scottish town, plus WELSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Irvine Welsh is the Edinburgh-born writer of Trainspotting.

clue.text: Aimless? I'm a disturbed Southern lady betrayed by both her lovers

definitions.text: Southern lady betrayed by both her lovers

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman from the American South, adrift and upset after both men in her life deceive her.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange AIMLESS and I'M A.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Amelia Evans is the heroine of Carson McCullers's The Ballad of the Sad Café, wronged by husband Marvin Macy and cousin Lymon.

clue.text: An archangel is a character from the past in a book with a Parisian present

definitions.text: a character from the past in a book with a Parisian present

parts.note: Michael is one of the archangels named in scripture

explanation.surface: Claims about a heavenly being who turns up as an old figure in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: MICHAEL, then IS as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Michaelis is a figure in both Conrad's The Secret Agent and Lawrence's Lady Chatterley's Lover.

clue.text: Struggle with wife's opinion

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A fight over what one's spouse thinks.
explanation.walkthrough: VIE plus W; the 's is 'has' linking the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is a personal belief or way of seeing a matter.

clue.text: Artist Vanessa's musical instrument

definitions.meaning: Vanessa ... was a Bloomsbury painter, sister of Virginia Woolf
a percussion instrument rung by striking

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive suggests something the painter owned; it is 'is' joining two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter Vanessa shares her surname with the ringing metal instrument found in churches and orchestras.

clue.text: I'm clear about an article that's made of clay

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the article

parts.note: to clear money is to earn it as net profit, so the speaker clears means earn
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone insists they have tidied up a piece of pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' here is the accounting sense: to make a net profit, as in clearing a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen describes pottery fired from baked earth such as clay.

clue.text: Melville character with a naval rank and some income, but no ship

parts.note: captain is a rank in the navy
a bob is an old British shilling, and a few bob means some money

explanation.surface: A Melville figure who holds a navy commission and has money but no vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But no ship' adds colour: in Omoo, Captain Bob is the old Tahitian jailer, a captain with no ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Bob is the genial native jailer of the mutinous sailors in Herman Melville's South Seas novel Omoo.

clue.text: Choice poetry came from this chap, an English emigrant with anguish

definitions.text: Choice poetry came from this chap

parts.note: a Pom is Australian slang for an English immigrant
fret means worry or anguish

explanation.surface: A fine poet who was a worried Englishman abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: POM (Australian slang for a Briton who has emigrated) and FRET; 'Choice' is the title of the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: John Pomfret's 1700 poem The Choice, about the ideal retired life, was one of the most popular of its age.

clue.text: Global Christian symbol? It is linked with royalty and it goes way over our heads

definitions.text: it goes way over our heads

parts.note: the orb, a globe topped with a cross, is part of the regalia
taken as written
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A cross-topped globe is a royal emblem, beyond our understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: ORB, IT, and ER for the monarch. 'Goes over our heads' suggests incomprehension, but means circles above.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiter is a spacecraft circling the earth, high above us.

clue.text: Sex goddess receiving lots of fallen heroes? Yes, Juliet's in distracted fear

definitions.text: Sex goddess receiving lots of fallen heroes?

indicators.note: in puts the two letters inside the jumbled word
distracted means confused or agitated, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Y is a short form of yes in texting
Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A goddess of love welcomes the warrior dead; yes, Juliet is in a state of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: FEAR jumbled ('distracted') to FREA holds Y and J.
explanation.definitionFit: Freyja is the Norse goddess of love, who takes half of the warriors slain in battle to her hall.

clue.text: A Shropshire lass in story ending with complex relationships Stoker's written about retrospectively

indicators.note: in puts the story ending and the web inside the reversed name
retrospectively means looking back, so the name is read in reverse

parts.note: Bram Stoker was the author of Dracula

indicators.note: ending points to the last letter of story

parts.note: a web is a complex network of relationships

explanation.surface: A country girl appears in a tale ending in tangled relationships, which the Dracula author looks back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospectively' turns the Dracula author's first name round; the last letter of 'story' and a web of relationships go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Webb was a novelist from Shropshire, author of Precious Bane, so a lass of that county.

clue.text: Part in drum and bass music

indicators.note: part in means only an inner portion of each word in the phrase is kept, the outer letters dropped

explanation.surface: A role in a genre of electronic dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the inner part of 'drum' and the front of 'bass', dropping D, AND and SS. 'Drum and bass' reads as the dance genre, steering away from the Cuban rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban dance and its music, with a distinctive syncopated rhythm.

clue.text: Contraception reportedly disastrous in a comedy

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: the pill is the oral contraceptive
grim means dire or disastrous

explanation.surface: Birth control said to be a calamity, in a funny play.
explanation.walkthrough: THE PILL said aloud plus GRIM makes the title of a Jacobean comedy by John Fletcher.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim is a comic play by John Fletcher, first staged around 1621.

clue.text: Mate in bed? That's crude and not allowed

indicators.note: not means the word for allowed is taken away

parts.note: a pallet is a crude straw mattress or makeshift bed
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Is a partner in bed rude and forbidden?
explanation.walkthrough: PALLET without LET ('allowed').
explanation.definitionFit: A pal is a friend or companion, as in a mate.

clue.text: "He capers nimbly in a lady's chamber / To the lascivious pleasing of a —" (Richard IIl)

definitions.text: "He capers nimbly in a lady's chamber / To the lascivious pleasing of a —" (Richard IIl)

parts.words: He capers nimbly in a lady's chamber / To the lascivious pleasing of a —" (Richard IIl)
parts.note: Gloucester's opening soliloquy mocks the courtier dancing to a stringed instrument in a lady's room

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from the opening speech of Richard III.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard of Gloucester sneers at peacetime amusement: dancing to the plucked instrument of love songs.

clue.text: Madly cherish elegant person who might help you solve the TLS crossword

definitions.text: person who might help you solve the TLS crossword

indicators.note: madly means wildly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wildly love a refined figure who could aid you with this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CHERISH ELEGANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher of literature and language would know the books and wordplay this literary puzzle needs.
